title: Clip a spring-gate carabiner to a steel tie-down staple
instruction: Clip the carabiner to the steel staple on the board, so the two are linked and the carabiner cannot be lifted off.
context: A spring-gate carabiner is clipped to an anchor by pushing its gate against the anchor's wire: the wire pushes the gate inward, passes through the opening, and the spring snaps the gate shut behind it. The wire has to meet the gate near its free end (the gate hinges at the other end), and the carabiner has to be moved square to the wire. Once the gate has closed the two are linked.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. A tie-down board (fixed, 200 x 340 mm, 8 mm thick, middle at x 0.31, y -0.20) carries a steel staple (fixed): two 6 mm legs 90 mm apart along y at x 0.345 (the near leg at y -0.22, the far one at y -0.13) joined by a 6 mm bar whose axis is 30 mm above the table. A key-ring carabiner (5 mm wire, 44 x 49 mm, 24 g, a gate on a revolute hinge with a 0.04 N m/rad spring, opening 60 degrees inward only) lies flat on the board with its spine at x 0.255, y -0.22 and its loop and gate pointing +x, toward the staple.
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each, judged as things stand at the end. (1) The carabiner was lifted at least 8 mm off the board at some time. (2) The near leg's axis passes through the carabiner's loop: it crosses the loop's plane inside the wires' centre line, between the board and 4 mm under the staple bar, the plane within 45 degrees of horizontal. (3) Clipped: step 2, the gate closed (within 3 degrees of shut), the carabiner lying on the board (spine within 8 mm of it, plane within 25 degrees of horizontal). (4) With step 3, no gripper pad is within 3 cm of the carabiner and none holds it. Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once all four steps have held together, without a break, for 1 s, with the carabiner within 2 mm and 2 degrees of where it was when that second began; any lapse restarts the second, and the step points stop at 0.8. A carabiner off the table scores 0 for the whole run.
reset_notes: Lay the carabiner flat on the board with its spine at x 0.255, y -0.22, its loop and gate toward +x and its gate closed; nothing else is moved.
fidelity: Rigid body plus a spring-hinged gate: capsule wires at true size (5 mm wire, 44 x 49 mm outline, 24 g), the gate as one capsule on a revolute joint with a spring (0.04 N m/rad) and damping; the nose is the joint's closed stop, with no hook or locking sleeve. The staple is fixed steel cylinders. Friction aluminium on steel 0.35 / 0.30. Real carabiner gates are stiffer (a few N at the gate); this one is light so that a 5 N push opens it.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2400 steps, hit the step limit); demo: 1.0 at step 332 (scripted demo, Isaac Lab-Arena)
